p.src: Jia Lian kept vigil at Pear-Fragrance Court for seven days and nights, while Buddhist and Taoist priests performed rites there without cease each day. Grandmother Jia summoned him and ordered that the coffin was not to be taken to the family temple. Jia Lian had no choice but to speak with Shijue again; they selected a grave above Third Sister You's and broke ground for the burial. On the day of the funeral, only members of the clan, Wang Xin and his wife, and Madam You with her daughters-in-law attended. Xifeng took no part in any of it and left him to make all the arrangements himself. With the year drawing to its close, countless duties were already piling up; on top of these, Lin Zhixiao submitted a list of eight unmarried manservants, all twenty-five and due to take wives and establish households, so that any maids within the household who were to be released might be matched with them. After reading it, Xifeng first went to consult Grandmother Jia and Lady Wang. They discussed the matter. Although several maids were of an age to be matched, each had some special circumstance: first, Yuanyang had sworn that she would not marry. Since that day, she had never spoken to Baoyu and no longer dressed herself in rich clothes or elaborate ornaments. Seeing how firm her resolve was, no one felt able to compel her. The second, Hupo, was ill and therefore could not be considered this time. Caiyun, having lately broken with Jia Huan, had also contracted an incurable illness. Only the senior maids who did rough work in Xifeng's and Li Wan's quarters were released; all the others were still too young. The men were therefore told to find wives outside the household.

p.src: For some time, Xifeng's illness had kept Li Wan and Tanchun so busy managing the household that they had no leisure; then the New Year and its festivals brought a host of miscellaneous affairs, and the poetry society was entirely set aside. Now that mid-spring had arrived, they had found some leisure; but Baoyu, afflicted in quick succession by Liu Xianglian's cold withdrawal from the world, Third Sister You's death by the sword, Second Sister You's death from swallowing gold, and Liu Wuer's illness brought on by anger, was beset by one idle sorrow and groundless grief after another, each arising before the last had passed. He became dazed in expression and manner, and often spoke incoherently, as though stricken with a disorder of the heart. Xiren and the others were alarmed, yet dared not report it to Grandmother Jia, and tried in every possible way to coax him into play and laughter.

p.src: Early one morning, just as he awoke, he heard an unending burst of giggles and chatter from the outer room. Xiren laughed and said, “Hurry out and rescue her! Qingwen and Sheyue have pinned Wendu down and are tickling her.” At this, Baoyu hurriedly threw on his grey squirrel-fur jacket and came out to look. The three girls had not yet folded their bedding or put on their outer clothes. Qingwen wore only a scallion-green silk jacket, red undergarments, and red sleeping slippers; her hair hung loose as she straddled Xiongnu. Sheyue, in a red satin breast-band with an old garment draped over her, was digging her fingers into Xiongnu's ribs. Xiongnu lay on her back on the kang, wearing a flower-sprigged close-fitting jacket, red trousers, and green socks. She kicked both feet wildly and laughed until she could scarcely breathe. Baoyu hurried forward and laughed. “Two big ones bullying one little one! Let me lend a hand.” With that, he climbed onto the bed and began tickling Qingwen. Qingwen, overcome by the tickling, laughingly let go of Xiongnu and grappled with Baoyu instead. Seizing her chance, Xiongnu pinned Qingwen down and began tickling her under the ribs. “Mind you don't catch cold,” Xiren said with a laugh. The sight of all four tangled together was exceedingly amusing.

p.src: Presently Li Wan sent Biyue over with a message: “Our mistress forgot a handkerchief here last night. Do you know whether it is still here?” “Yes, yes, it is!” said Xiaoyan. “I picked it up from the floor, but didn't know whose it was. I've just washed it and hung it out; it isn't dry yet.” Seeing the four of them tumbling about, Biyue laughed. “It certainly is lively here! At the crack of dawn you're already romping together amid all this giggling and chatter.” “There are plenty of people at your place too,” Baoyu said with a laugh. “Why don't you play together?” “Our mistress doesn't play,” replied Biyue, “and she keeps the two young ladies and Miss Baoqin constrained as guests as well. Now Miss Baoqin has gone to stay with the Old Lady again, so it is lonelier still. The two young ladies will remain through this year. By next winter they will both be gone, and then it will be lonelier than ever. Just look at Miss Baochai's place: since Xiangling left, how much quieter it has become, leaving Miss Xiangyun all alone.”

p.src: While they were speaking, Xiangyun sent Cuilü over with another message: “Second Master is requested to come out quickly and see a fine poem.” “Where is this fine poem?” Baoyu asked at once. Cuilü laughed. “The young ladies are all at Dripping Fragrance Pavilion. You will know when you get there.” At this, Baoyu hurriedly washed and dressed and went out. Sure enough, Daiyu, Baochai, Xiangyun, Baoqin, and Tanchun were all there, holding a poem and reading it. When they saw him, they all laughed and said, “Still not out of bed at this hour? Our poetry society has been disbanded for a whole year, and no one has done anything to revive it. Now it is early spring and all things are renewed; this is just the time to rouse ourselves and establish it afresh.” Xiangyun laughed. “When we first founded the poetry society, it was autumn, so naturally it could not flourish. But now all things are meeting the spring, a season that presages growth and abundance. Besides, this poem on peach blossoms is so fine that we should rename the Crabapple Society the Peach Blossom Society.” Baoyu listened, nodded, and said, “An excellent idea.” Then he eagerly asked to see the poem. The others said, “Let us go now and call on the Old Farmer of Sweet-Rice Village, so that we may all settle the matter properly.” With that, they all rose and made their way to Sweet-Rice Village. p.src: Baoyu read it without a word of praise, but tears rolled down his cheeks. He knew at once that it was Daiyu's work, and that was why he wept; fearing the others might see, he hastily wiped his tears away. Then he asked, “Where did you get this?” Baoqin laughed. “Guess who wrote it.” Baoyu smiled. “Naturally, it is a manuscript by the Master of the Xiaoxiang.” Baoqin laughed. “But I am the one who wrote it.” Baoyu laughed. “I do not believe you. The tone and manner are utterly unlike the style of Hengwu, so I cannot believe it.” Baochai laughed. “That only shows how little you understand. Do you suppose Du Fu wrote nothing in every poem but lines like ‘Twice have chrysanthemums bloomed, bringing tears for other days’! He also wrote such charming lines as ‘Red blossoms burst on the rain-plumped plum’ and ‘Water-plants tug in the wind at their long green ribbons.’” Baoyu smiled. “That is true enough. But I know you would never permit your younger cousin to write such mournful lines; and talented though she is, she would certainly never choose to write them. She is not like Cousin Lin, who has suffered bereavement and separation and so could give voice to such sorrow.” At this, everyone laughed.

p.src: By then they had reached Paddy-Sweet Cottage. They showed the poem to Li Wan, who naturally praised it without end. When the poetry club was mentioned, they all agreed to reconvene the next day, the second of the third month, renaming the Crab-Flower Club the Peach Blossom Club and making Lin Daiyu its president. They would all gather at Xiaoxiang Lodge after the midday meal. They then began proposing subjects. Daiyu said, “Let us each write a hundred-rhyme poem on peach blossoms.” Baochai replied, “That will not do. There have always been so many poems on peach blossoms that anything we write is bound to be conventional; it cannot compare with this old-style poem of yours. We must think of something else.” While they were still speaking, a servant announced, “Your aunt has arrived. The young ladies are requested to come out and pay their respects.” They therefore all went to the front rooms to greet Wang Ziteng's wife and keep her company in conversation. After the meal, they accompanied her into the garden and made a tour of its various sights. She did not leave until the lamps were lit after the evening meal.

p.src: The next day was Tanchun's birthday, and Yuanchun had already sent two young eunuchs with several playthings as gifts. It goes without saying that everyone in the household had a birthday gift for her. After the meal, Tanchun changed into ceremonial dress and went around paying her respects. Daiyu said to the others with a smile, “My timing in reopening this club is unfortunate again. I completely forgot that her birthday fell around now. Even though there will be no banquet or opera, we must all spend the day amusing her in Grandmother's and Aunt's presence, so how could we find any leisure?” The meeting was therefore postponed to the fifth.

p.src: That day, after the young ladies had all attended the morning meal in the inner apartments, a letter arrived from Jia Zheng. After paying his respects, Baoyu opened the message addressed to Grandmother Jia and read it aloud to her. It contained little beyond greetings and the news that he expected to enter the capital in the middle of the sixth month. The remaining family letters and memoranda concerning household business were naturally opened and read by Jia Lian and Lady Wang. Everyone was overjoyed to hear that he would return to the capital in the sixth or seventh month. Just then, however, Wang Ziteng's daughter had been betrothed to the son of the Marquis of Baoning, and the tenth day of the fifth month had been chosen for her wedding. Xifeng was so busy making the arrangements that she was often away from home for three or five days at a time. That day Wang Ziteng's wife came once more to fetch Xifeng and invited all her nephews and nieces as well, to spend a pleasant day with her. Grandmother Jia and Lady Wang ordered Baoyu, Tanchun, Lin Daiyu, and Baochai to accompany Xifeng. None of them dared disobey, so they had no choice but to return to their rooms and dress themselves afresh. The five took their leave, spent the day away, and did not return until the lamps were lit. Baoyu returned to Happy Red Court and rested for a short while. Taking advantage of the occasion, Aroma urged him to settle his mind and use his spare time to put his books in order and prepare himself. Baoyu counted on his fingers and said, “There is plenty of time yet.” Aroma said, “Your books come first, but your calligraphy comes second. Even if you have mastered the books by then, where will you find enough samples of your handwriting?” Baoyu laughed. “I have often written quite a lot. Surely none of it has been kept?” “Of course it has,” Aroma replied. “Yesterday, while you were away, I took it all out and counted it. There were only fifty or sixty sheets. Surely three or four years' work cannot amount to no more than those few sheets of calligraphy. In my opinion, beginning tomorrow you should put every other concern aside and quickly copy several sheets each day to make up the number. Even if you cannot produce the full amount for every single day, the total should at least look roughly credible.” On hearing this, Baoyu hurriedly inspected the collection himself once more. Finding that there was truly no way to bluff his way through, he said, “Starting tomorrow, I had better write a hundred characters a day.” After this conversation, they all settled down for the night. The next morning, as soon as he had risen and washed, Baoyu ground ink beneath the window and began carefully copying a calligraphy model in a formal hand. When Grandmother Jia did not see him, she assumed that he was ill and hurriedly sent someone to inquire. Only then did Baoyu go to pay his respects. He explained that he had been practicing calligraphy, intending to devote the early morning hours to it before doing anything else, and that this was why he had come out late. Grandmother Jia was delighted to hear this and instructed him, “From now on, you may simply stay in and practice calligraphy and read; you need not come out at all. Go and inform your mother.” Baoyu obeyed and went to Lady Wang's room to explain the matter. Lady Wang said, “Sharpening your spear only when the battle is upon you will be of no use. If you had shown this urgency before and read and written every day, how much might you not have finished by now? Now you will drive yourself so hard that you will end by making yourself ill.” Baoyu replied that it would do him no harm.

p.src: Lin Daiyu had heard that, when Jia Zheng returned home, he would be sure to question Baoyu about his studies; if Baoyu allowed himself to be distracted, she feared he would suffer when the time came. She therefore merely pretended to have lost interest, refrained from reconvening the poetry club, and did not tempt him away with outside diversions. Tanchun and Baochai each copied out a page of regular script for Baoyu every day, while Baoyu himself worked harder too, writing two or three hundred characters daily as the case might be. By the latter part of the third month, he had thus amassed a considerable quantity of calligraphy. That day he calculated that, with another fifty sheets, he could just about muddle through. Just then Zijuan came and gave Baoyu a roll of papers. When he opened it, he found page after page of tiny regular script in the styles of Zhong and Wang, copied on aged, oiled bamboo paper; the handwriting closely resembled his own. Overjoyed, Baoyu bowed deeply to Zijuan and then went in person to offer his thanks. Shi Xiangyun and Baoqin likewise copied several sheets apiece and sent them to him. Although the collected sheets did not fully meet the assignment, they were enough to pass muster. Relieved, Baoyu then reviewed several times the books he was expected to study. While he was applying himself every day, it happened that a tidal disaster struck the coastal region and devastated several inhabited districts. The local officials submitted a memorial reporting the disaster, whereupon an imperial decree ordered Jia Zheng to inspect the affected region and administer relief on his way home. By this reckoning, he would not return until the end of winter. When Baoyu heard this, he set his books and calligraphy aside once more and went back to idling about as before.

p.src: When the others arrived, they saw that the subject was willow catkins and that various short lyric forms had been prescribed. They all read Shi Xiangyun’s lyric as well and praised it for some time. Baoyu laughed. “We are not much practiced in lyric writing, but I suppose we shall have to scribble something all the same.” They then drew lots: Baochai drew “Immortal by the River,” Baoqin “Moon over the Western River,” Tanchun “Song of the Southern Bough,” Daiyu “Long Song of Tang,” and Baoyu “Butterflies in Love with Flowers.” Zijuan lit a stick of Sweet-Dream incense, and everyone began to ponder. Before long, Daiyu found her inspiration and finished writing. Baoqin and Baochai followed soon afterward. When the three had finished and were about to read one another’s work, Baochai laughed. “Let me finish reading yours before you look at mine.” Tanchun laughed. “Oh dear, why is the incense burning so quickly today? Only a third remains. I have composed only half a lyric.” She then asked whether Baoyu had finished. p.src: Before she had finished speaking, there came a crash from the bamboo outside the window, as though a window lattice had fallen, startling everyone. When the maids went out to look, a maid beyond the curtain cried, “A large butterfly kite has caught on the tip of the bamboo!” The maids laughed. “What a beautifully made kite! I wonder whose string broke. Take it down.” Hearing this, Baoyu and the others came out to look as well. Baoyu laughed. “I recognize this kite. Miss Jiaohong from the Elder Master’s household was flying it. Take it down and send it back to her.” Zijuan laughed. “Surely there can be two identical kites in the world. Is she the only one allowed to own such a thing? I do not care—I am keeping it for now.” “Zijuan is learning to be possessive too,” said Tanchun. You have kites of your own, yet now you want to keep one someone else has let fly away. Aren’t you afraid of the ill omen?” Daiyu laughed. “Quite right. Who knows whose misfortune was sent off with it? Throw it out at once. Bring ours out, and we shall send our misfortunes away too.” At this, Zijuan promptly ordered the young maids to take the kite to the old women on duty at the garden gate, so that it could be returned if anyone came looking for it.

p.src: When the young maids heard that they were going to fly kites, they eagerly bustled about and brought out a kite shaped like a beautiful woman. Some fetched a tall stool, some fastened the forked line, and others unwound the reel. Baochai and the others stood before the courtyard gate and told the maids to fly it in the open ground outside. Baoqin laughed. “That one of yours is not very pretty. Third Sister’s great soft-winged phoenix is much better.” “Indeed it is,” Baochai agreed with a smile. Then she turned to Cuimo and said with a smile, “Bring yours out and fly it too.” Cuimo grinned and went to fetch it. Baoyu’s enthusiasm rose too. He sent a young maid back to his quarters, saying, “Bring me the big fish Madam Lai gave me yesterday.” After a long while, the young maid returned empty-handed and said with a smile, “Miss Qing let it fly away yesterday.” “But I never flew it even once,” said Baoyu. Tanchun laughed. “In any case, she only sent your misfortunes away for you.” “Very well,” said Baoyu. Then bring me the big crab.” The maid went and returned with several others carrying a beauty kite and its reel. “Miss Xiren says the crab was given to Third Master yesterday. This one was just sent over by Madam Lin. Fly this instead.” Baoyu examined it closely and found the figure exquisitely made. Delighted, he ordered them to launch it. By then Tanchun’s kite had also been brought, and Cuimo and several young maids had already launched it on the hillside opposite. Baoqin also ordered someone to fetch her own large red bat kite. Baochai, caught up in the fun, had hers brought too: seven wild geese joined in a row. Soon all the kites were aloft. Only Baoyu’s beauty kite refused to rise. Baoyu said the maids did not know how to fly it and tried himself for a long while, but it rose no higher than the roof before falling again. Baoyu grew so anxious that sweat broke out on his brow, making everyone laugh again. In vexation, Baoyu flung it to the ground and pointed at it. “If you were not a beauty, I would stamp you to pieces!” Daiyu laughed. “The bridle line is badly set. Take it out and have someone reset it, and it will fly properly.” Baoyu sent it away to have the bridle line reset, while another kite was fetched for him to fly. Everyone looked upward; the several kites were now soaring high in the sky.

p.src: Presently the maids brought out many kites of assorted designs to send up alongside the others, and everyone played for a while. Zijuan laughed. “This one pulls hard. Miss, you fly it.” Hearing this, Daiyu protected her hand with a handkerchief and tested the line. The wind was indeed strong and the pull powerful. Taking the reel, she let it spin with the kite’s momentum; it rattled loudly, and in an instant all the line had run out. Daiyu then invited the others to take a turn. They all laughed. “We each have one of our own. You go first.” Daiyu smiled. “It is amusing to let it go, but I cannot bear to do it.” Li Wan said, “That is the very pleasure of flying kites. That is why they call it sending away misfortune. You of all people should release several more, so they may carry the root of your illness away with them.” Zijuan laughed. “Our young lady grows more possessive by the day. Every year she lets several go, but today she has suddenly taken pity on one. If you will not release it, Miss, I shall.” With that, she took a small pair of Western silver scissors from Xueyan and, leaving not an inch of line at the base of the reel, snipped it clean through. “There—it will carry the very root of your illness away!” she said with a laugh. The kite drifted and swayed, receding steadily. Soon it was no larger than an egg; in another instant it was only a black speck, and then it vanished altogether. Everyone squinted upward and cried, “What fun! What fun!” Baoyu said, “What a pity we do not know where it will fall. If it comes down in an inhabited place and a child finds it, all will be well. But if it falls in some deserted wilderness, I shall feel lonely on its behalf. Come to think of it, I shall let mine go too, so the two can keep each other company.” So he too cut the line with the scissors and released his kite in the same way. Tanchun was just about to cut loose her phoenix when she saw another phoenix in the sky. “I wonder whose that is,” she said. Everyone laughed. “Do not cut yours yet. That one looks as though it means to tangle with it.” As they spoke, the other phoenix drew gradually nearer and tangled with Tanchun’s. Just as they began reeling in their line, the people at the other end did the same, and neither side could free itself. Then another kite approached—a filigree character for “double happiness,” as large as a door panel and fitted with a whistling firecracker, booming in midair like a bell. Everyone laughed. “This one has come to join the tangle too. Do not reel in yet. It will be amusing to let all three tangle together.” As they spoke, the “double happiness” kite duly tangled with the two phoenixes. All three parties tugged and jerked at once, until suddenly every line snapped, and the three kites drifted and swayed away together. Everyone clapped and burst into laughter. “That was great fun! But whose was the ‘double happiness’ kite? What a mischievous trick to play!”
